# @amykit/plugin-prove

Proves a phase against the real system: one workflow walks the scenario each brief settled, through the operations the mounted plugins offer.

A workflow for [amy](https://github.com/nicolasmelo1/amy): a diagram of where work can go, a
decision per state saying where it goes next, and the actions that happen in the world. The
engine drives it without knowing what any of its states mean.

Use it as the proving phase of a project, once a brief has settled the scenario the work must pass. It is a workflow that walks that scenario against the real system through the operations mounted plugins offer, such as agent-browser, agent-desktop and terminal, and records a proof. It needs file-brief-store and a notifier; mount command for the resources a scenario runs against and the code digest, and a conversation so it can ask a person to make a fixture hold.

## What it extends

|  |  |
| :-- | :-- |
| Ports | _none_ |
| Actions | _none_ |
| Operations | `prove.record`, `prove.show` |
| Commands | `amy prove record`, `amy prove show` |
| Events | _none_ |
| Environment | _none_ |

## Calling it

It takes an input, so it is called from a state of another workflow rather than mounted
as a profile. Depend on it from the package that calls it, mark the state `call` in that
workflow's diagram, draw an edge out of it named for each end (`refused`, `PROVEN`), and bind it:

```ts
import { plugin as prove } from "@amykit/plugin-prove";

calls: { STATE: call(prove, { input: (work) => ({ /* … */ }) }) },
```

Its settings below are set per call site, with `config` on the binding.

## The lifecycle

| State | Kind |
| :-- | :-- |
| `READING` | initial, waiting |
| `LEASING` | waiting |
| `PREPARING` | working |
| `refused` | terminal |
| `RUNNING` | working |
| `ASKING` | waiting |
| `PROVEN` | terminal |

It emits `ask`, `finish`, `give-up`, `lease`, `prepare`, `renew` and `run-step`.

## Configuration

```ts
call(prove, { config: { digest: "", fixtures: {}, policy: { askEveryMs: 60000, fixtureDeadlineMs: 86400000, leaseTtlMs: 600000, seatRetryMs: 30000 }, resources: {} } })
```

| Setting | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `digest` | `string` | no | `""` | the command, by the name the commands port allows, that prints the digest of the code a proof certifies. Empty where the unit has no code |
| `fixtures` | `record` | no | `{}` | states a scenario starts from, shared by name: `{ ensure: [{ check: { operation, input, expect }, act: { operation, input } }] }` |
| `policy.askEveryMs` | `number` | no | `60000` | how often a run waiting on a person looks for the answer |
| `policy.fixtureDeadlineMs` | `number` | no | `86400000` | how long a person has to make a fixture hold before the run gives up |
| `policy.leaseTtlMs` | `number` | no | `600000` | how long a seat on a resource lasts without its run renewing it |
| `policy.seatRetryMs` | `number` | no | `30000` | how long a run waits before asking again for a seat or a scenario |
| `resources` | `record` | no | `{}` | what a scenario runs against, by name: `{ capacity, up, check, down }`, each a command the commands port allows. `check` is required |

Every field is checked at boot against the schema this package declares. A key that is
not one of the above is a refusal naming the plugin and the key, not a setting that
silently never applied.

## What it brings

| Command | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| `amy prove record` | Record a scenario a person ran by hand as the unit's proof |
| `amy prove show` | Say whether a unit is proven for the code and brief it is at now |

Typed on a machine that mounted this package, and unknown on one that did not.

    %% One proving walk for every scenario. The scenario is the input, so a
    %% single request and two apps with a fixture and a person differ in data
    %% alone, never in this diagram. Dashed states wait as looks, spending no
    %% attempt: for a brief that names a scenario, for a seat on a resource.
    %% ASKING keeps its seats while a person answers, and gives them back at
    %% its deadline. Every end releases what the run held.
    classDef waiting stroke-dasharray: 4 4
    classDef attention stroke-width:3px

    [*] --> READING
    READING --> LEASING: the brief names a scenario
    LEASING --> PREPARING: every resource it needs is leased
    LEASING --> refused: it needs a resource nobody configured
    PREPARING --> RUNNING: the resources are up and the fixtures hold
    PREPARING --> ASKING: a fixture cannot reach its state
    PREPARING --> LEASING: a lease ran out
    PREPARING --> refused: a resource failed its check
    RUNNING --> ASKING: a human step
    RUNNING --> LEASING: a lease ran out
    RUNNING --> PROVEN: every assertion passed
    RUNNING --> refused: an assertion failed or could not be evaluated
    ASKING --> RUNNING: the person answered the step
    ASKING --> PREPARING: the person made the fixture hold
    ASKING --> LEASING: a lease ran out
    ASKING --> refused: nobody answered before the deadline
    PROVEN --> [*]
    refused --> [*]

    class READING,LEASING waiting
    class ASKING attention
